title: A Theory of How Pretraining Shapes Inductive Bias in Fine-Tuning
claim: The studied setting is a two-stage diagonal network whose behavior depends on initialization parameters and on how pretraining and fine-tuning task structure overlap.
layout: 3 panels: networks on top, teacher vectors and parameter table below, color-coded
description: Panel a shows two side-by-side diagonal linear networks, one titled Pretraining (PT) and one Fine-tuning (FT). Each has six grayscale input nodes linked one-to-one to six hidden nodes, with the weights labeled w. The hidden nodes converge on a single black output node through weights labeled v. Solid and dotted lines mark positive and negative weight branches. The effective predictor is written below each network as β̂ = w ∘ v. Panel b shows PT Teacher and FT Teacher as vertical columns of squares. Active dimensions are green for PT, blue for dimensions shared with PT in FT, and purple for new dimensions in FT. Inactive dimensions are gray. Panel c has a pink box listing the initialization parameters c_PT, λ_PT and γ_FT with their formulas. Below it, a gray box defines the task parameters ρ_PT, ρ_FT^shared and ρ_FT^new, each matched to a color swatch. The eye goes first to the two networks, then to the pink box.
caption: Setup. Schematic illustration of the theoretical setup: dependence on the initialization parameters $c_{PT}$, $\lambda_{PT}$, and $\gamma_{FT}$ (shown in pink); and dependence on the data parameters $\rho_{PT}$, $\rho_{FT}^{shared}$, and $\rho_{FT}^{new}$ (shown in grey).
abstract: Pretraining and fine-tuning are central stages in modern machine learning systems. In practice, feature learning plays an important role across both stages: deep neural networks learn a broad range of useful features during pretraining and further refine those features during fine-tuning. However, an end-to-end theoretical understanding of how choices of initialization impact the ability to reuse and refine features during fine-tuning has remained elusive. Here we develop an analytical theory of the pretraining fine-tuning pipeline in diagonal linear networks, deriving exact expressions for the generalization error as a function of initialization parameters and task statistics. We find that different initialization choices place the network into four distinct fine-tuning regimes that are distinguished by their ability to support feature learning and reuse and therefore by the task statistics for which they are beneficial. In particular, a smaller initialization scale in earlier layers enables the network to both reuse and refine its features, leading to superior generalization on fine-tuning tasks that rely on a subset of pretraining features. We demonstrate empirically that the same initialization parameters impact generalization in ResNets trained on CIFAR-100 and SVHN as well as Transformers trained on modular arithmetic tasks. Overall, our results demonstrate an alytically how data and network initialization interact to shape fine-tuning generalization, highlighting an important role for the relative scale of initialization across different layers in enabling continued feature learning during fine-tuning.
